description: TinyDispatcher is a small, compile-time oriented dispatcher for .NET with pipelines and source generation.
releaseNotes:
<PropertyGroup><PackageReleaseNotes><PackageReleaseNotes>
            Performance: optimized middleware pipeline execution (significantly reduced allocations in the dispatch path).

            Breaking: middleware contract updated (see migration below).

            <h2>Pipeline Hardening & Performance Refactor (Breaking Changes)</h2>

            <p>
            This prerelease delivers a major redesign of the TinyDispatcher pipeline execution model.
            Generated pipelines are now switch-runner based with constructor-injected middleware,
            reducing allocations and improving readability of the generated code.
            </p>

            <h3>What changed</h3>
            <ul>
            <li>Replaced delegate-chaining pipelines with switch-based generated pipelines (runtime runner).</li>
            <li>Middleware is now constructor-injected into generated pipelines (DI-friendly, more readable code).</li>
            <li>Deterministic middleware layering is enforced consistently:
            <strong>Global → Policy → Per-command → Handler</strong>.
            </li>
            <li>Benchmarks updated and validated in Release mode.</li>
            </ul>

            <h3>Breaking changes (Middleware API)</h3>

            <p>
            <strong>CommandDelegate has been removed</strong> and middleware now uses a runtime interface.
            </p>

            <p><strong>Old signature:</strong></p>
            <pre>
            Task InvokeAsync(
            TCommand command,
            TContext context,
            CommandDelegate<TCommand, TContext> next,
            CancellationToken ct);
            </pre>

            <p><strong>New signature:</strong></p>
            <pre>
            ValueTask InvokeAsync(
            TCommand command,
            TContext context,
            Pipeline.ICommandPipelineRuntime<TCommand, TContext> runtime,
            CancellationToken ct);
            </pre>

            <h3>Migration guide</h3>

            <p>Replace:</p>
            <pre>
            await next(command, context, ct);
            </pre>

            <p>With:</p>
            <pre>
            await runtime.NextAsync(command, context, ct);
            </pre>

            <p>If your middleware only forwards execution:</p>
            <pre>
            public ValueTask InvokeAsync(
            TCommand command,
            TContext context,
            Pipeline.ICommandPipelineRuntime<TCommand, TContext> runtime,
            CancellationToken ct)
            => runtime.NextAsync(command, context, ct);
            </pre>

            <h2>Pipeline Contract Simplification (Breaking)</h2>

            <p>
            The dispatcher no longer performs runtime pipeline precedence resolution.
            Global, Policy, and Per-command pipelines are now unified under a single
            <code>ICommandPipeline<TCommand,TContext></code> contract.
            </p>

            <h3>What changed</h3>
            <ul>
            <li>Removed <code>IPolicyCommandPipeline<,></code>.</li>
            <li>Removed <code>IGlobalCommandPipeline<,></code>.</li>
            <li>Dispatcher now resolves a single <code>ICommandPipeline<TCommand,TContext></code>.</li>
            <li>Pipeline precedence (Per-command → Policy → Global) is enforced at compile-time by source generation.</li>
            <li>Reduced DI lookups and removed runtime branching in the dispatch path.</li>
            </ul>

            <h3>Migration guide</h3>
            <p>
            If you were implementing <code>IPolicyCommandPipeline<,></code> or
            <code>IGlobalCommandPipeline<,></code>, replace them with
            <code>ICommandPipeline<TCommand,TContext></code>.
            </p>

            <h3>Notes</h3>
            <ul>
            <li>This change simplifies the public API surface and reduces runtime complexity.</li>
            <li>Pipeline resolution is now deterministic and fully generator-driven.</li>
            <li>This is part of the final hardening phase toward v1.0.</li>
            </ul>
          </PackageReleaseNotes></PackageReleaseNotes></PropertyGroup>
